gates.name: restart_phase_recorded
gates.note: Deliberately weak: this asserts the KEY exists (the additive-migration invariant — an older deployment gains the field), not that a restart happened. It therefore passes on a zero-write run and proves nothing about a restart transition. The transition itself is checked by restart_transition_recorded below.

content_lint.name: spoken_no_machinery
content_lint.forbid: \b(restart_phase|restart_queue|restart_clean_weeks|restart_system|setup_status|current_stage|completed_stages|pushback_calibration|triggered_active|insufficient_dose|insufficient_time|mechanism_wrong|metric_wrong|goal_wrong|check_frequency|monitored_signal|response_evidence|min_test_duration|expected_signal|decision_rule|stabilizing|reintroducing|STATE\.md|the state file|the restart machine|the queue|the system under evaluation|clean-week count)\b
content_lint.note: The register class, made deterministic. The machinery leak was fixed twice and moved each time — prose (v0.2.2) -> the pulse recap (v0.2.3) -> the queue offer. Patching each instance never killed the class, because catching the next hiding place always required a judge to read for it. This runs against spoken.md (assistant turns verbatim, nothing else) rather than transcript.md ON PURPOSE: the runner's own transcript annotations name state files and fields, and a lint cannot tell the runner's voice from the plugin's — linting transcript.md false-positived on adv-out-of-order/run-2, whose register the judges had confirmed clean. It is a vocabulary blacklist rather than a rule about intent, because three iterations proved the leak survives any rule phrased as advice about how to talk. optional_file: n/a on pre-iteration-4 captures, which predate spoken.md.

content_lint.name: state_no_placeholders
content_lint.note: FILL is deliberately absent here though active.md forbids it: `**Direction:** [FILL]` is a sanctioned init-template value for a Direction the user has not given yet. In active.md the same token is residue. Four iteration-2 judges flagged the asymmetry as a bug; it is not.
